note: Skeptical-researcher pass only. Fresh context from this draft text alone. Severity kept to findings that would falsify a North-Star claim or leave a success criterion un-disprovable as written.

findings.section: Phase 1 D-A; Success criteria (real execution + validated handback); Phase 8
findings.criterion: Anchor executes a confirmed commission as a real trio run and the produced plan/handback is usable; no changes to Crucible/Foreman/researchPrime
findings.message: D-A locks adapter-side extraction and then defines `absent` on `uncertainty_flags` or `human_wait` as REFUSAL—before any sample of what real Crucible/Foreman artifacts actually contain. Under that rule, if the trio’s existing journals/halts/budgets do not already emit those facts, every real handback is refused and criterion 3 can never go green without either synthesizing (banned for those fields) or teaching the trio (non-goal). A skeptical researcher would refuse this decision until Phase 0 includes a field-by-field extractability matrix over real on-disk trio outputs, with measured rates of observed vs absent. Locking refusal semantics first is deciding the verdict before reading the evidence.

findings.criterion: Nothing is spent, written, or started without a human confirmation; campaign ledger is single source of truth
findings.message: Criterion 1 and Phase 6 have a spoken/typed description compile into a durable Face north-star, roadmap steps, size classes, and commissionability flags—with zero chat turns—but never route that first durable write through propose→confirm or any other explicit human confirmation. The North Star’s “nothing … written … without a human confirmation” is broader than “nothing spent.” If Face + Campaign Roadmap are the ledger, standing them up is a ledger write. As written, the plan can GREEN “fresh start” by silently materializing the campaign truth John never confirmed. Either Face commit is a confirmed act (name the confirm surface and `who`), or the North Star’s “written” clause is being narrowed without an amendment.

findings.section: Phase 1 D-B; Phase 2 REAL-SUBSTRATE GATE; Phase 10
findings.criterion: Campaign ledger remains the single source of truth; single writer proven as a storage claim
findings.message: D-B makes the authoritative ledger local/non-synced and says boot refuses unsupported (synced/OneDrive) paths—synced is export only. Phase 2 then makes the concurrency/crash gate required on “an actual synced Windows path,” and Phase 10 re-runs criterion 7 there. That is a substrate contradiction: either production never runs on the path you treat as the real proof (so a green synced test is a false receipt for the product), or production does run on synced storage (so D-B is false and the SSOT can be corrupted by the class of failure you claim to ban). Skeptical standard: durability evidence must be collected on the substrate the boot path actually allows—local WAL under the supported path—not on the path the product is forbidden to use.

findings.section: Phase 1 falsify classifyArtifact; Phase 8 artifact card; Success criteria (reviewable artifact)
findings.criterion: Produced plan is an artifact John can read on screen; no bespoke plan template (Crucible plan shape IS the template)
findings.message: Phase 0 correctly demands a live falsification against a real doc-trio “today” and to paste the ACTUAL result into the plan. The draft under review still contains neither the output nor a locked consequence (a vs b). Downstream Phase 8 already designs as if option (a) DOC-TRIO MANIFEST will honor the non-goal. That is planning on a hoped-for experimental outcome. If classification already fails, option (a) may be a new presentation template in packaging clothing; option (b) needs an explicit North-Star amendment. Until the paste exists, criterion 4 and the non-goal are both open risks, not closed Phase-0 work.

findings.criterion: Project driven BY TALKING TO ITS STEWARD (with D-D’s proposed scope of talking)
findings.message: Success criteria and later phases repeatedly require “spoken description,” “spoken correction,” and Phase 10 “spoken correction” acceptance, while D-D proposes amending talking to typed conversational dialogue and parking speech-to-text. The draft does not apply that amendment to the criteria it will be scored against. A Stage-2 plan that still says “spoken” will either over-build audio or fail acceptance on vocabulary. Skeptical fix: rewrite every success criterion and acceptance scenario in the locked modality before claiming D-D is cheap insurance—or drop D-D and own speech as in-scope.

findings.section: Phase 1 D-C; Phase 6 commissionability and size class
findings.criterion: Nothing that makes the steward do the planning itself rather than commission it; steward compiles description into Face and Roadmap, then proposes commissions
findings.message: D-C draws a WHAT/WHY vs HOW bright line, then Phase 6 has the compile assign size class, decide commissionability, and split non-commissionable steps at compile time. That is decomposition and scoping of work—the HOW of campaign structure—performed by the steward path without a Crucible commission. The non-goal is not only “no wave list inside a step”; it is that the steward must not become the planner. As written, a “smart compile” can invent the roadmap shape John only meant as raw intent. Either commissionability/size-class are deferred to a commissioned planning step, or each is justified in the decision log as still-not-planning with a falsifiable lint that cannot smuggle sequencing or acceptance criteria under new names.

findings.section: Phase 4 lease liveness; Phase 9 park/restart/kill; Success criteria (honest status)
findings.criterion: Roadmap shows the truth about what is running (park, restart, kill)
findings.message: Liveness is proven by “SIGKILL, not graceful shutdown,” plus machine-reboot/OOM variants. This draft does not define the Windows-real kill mechanism (taskkill /F, TerminateProcess, job-object kill) or how lease expiry is observed under ConPTY/supervisor topology. SIGKILL is a POSIX claim. If the acceptance test cannot be executed as named on the host the product runs on, criterion 5 is not falsifiable. Specify the OS-native hard-kill and assert `lost` within the lease window under that kill—not a Unix metaphor.

findings.topic: budget ceiling enforcement without trio changes
findings.section: Phase 7 real budget in the runner
findings.criterion: Nothing spent without confirmation; no changes to Crucible/Foreman/researchPrime
findings.message: Phase 7 requires token/agent-count/wall-clock ceilings enforced by “the process that owns the run, not by the trio,” with halt + re-confirm on breach. The draft never names the enforcement mechanism (wrapper kill, cgroup/job object, argv flags, polling). External hard-stop can leave trio state corrupt or un-resumable; argv flags risk trio changes or auto-approve-like surfaces already banned. Without a measured, no-trio-source mechanism, this is either an untestable promise or a stealth amendment to the non-goal. Skeptical standard: name the kill/pause primitive, the resume story after budget halt, and a test that spend stops without trio patches.

findings.criterion: Nothing spent/started without confirmation, proven with auth ON on outcomes (surface already shipped broken auth-off)
findings.message: The plan elevates ANCHOR_TOKEN-set tests because “this surface shipped broken twice,” but Phase 0 inventories gates and start paths—not why auth-off was the effective default (test harness defaults, missing middleware, query-string tokens, SSE unchecked, CI env). Making auth-ON the default test mode without a root-cause inventory re-tests the symptom. Skeptical researcher demand: Phase 0 AUTH-FAILURE inventory (each bypass class + disposition) beside START-PATH inventory; acceptance maps each historical failure class to a regression that fails closed when auth is on.

findings.criterion: Commission proposed for a named roadmap step; nothing runs until John confirms; confirmation records who
findings.message: Citing `proposeCommission (141) / confirmCommission (250)` as “engine halves already exist” is not evidence those functions bind to a named roadmap step, mint single-use tokens, record `who`, or refuse unauthenticated spend. Line numbers are not behavioral contracts; they can be stubs, auth-off only, or free-floating commissions. Phase 3 redesigns the choke point as if greenfield anyway—so the “already exist” claim either understates required rewrite or overstates readiness. Replace with a Phase-0 behavioral table: inputs, outputs, auth posture, step-binding, and a failing test list against current code—or drop the existence claim.

findings.section: Phase 5; Phase 10 criterion 3; Success criteria (real execution; when he says start, Foreman executes)
findings.criterion: Real trio run; when John says start, Foreman executes; Roadmap shows truth
findings.message: The only required real engine cycle is one Crucible HALT→confirm→resume. Foreman blocker inventory is listed in Phase 0, then deferred as “unknown halts until observed.” researchPrime is essentially absent. North Star and success criteria say trio/Foreman execution, not “Crucible stage gates only.” A system that only proves Crucible human gates can still lie or refuse on Foreman park/restart/kill and research commissions. At minimum, Phase 10 must require one real Foreman start path (or an explicit North-Star narrowing to “Crucible first, Foreman later”) and a disposition for researchPrime commissions—not an implied trio from one engine’s approve gates.

findings.section: Phase 2 single writer and Python outbox; Phase 9 status_flip; Success criteria (honest status; single writer)
findings.criterion: Roadmap shows the truth about what is running; campaign ledger single source of truth
findings.message: Python may not write `roadmap_events` but it owns an outbox the Node writer drains. The hardening receipt covers writer WAL commit and racing writers on the Node side; it does not name atomicity for “status change durable in outbox” → “ordered event visible to projection,” nor crash between append and drain, nor Node-down while a run continues. Criterion 5 fails if the process is dead/`lost` but the Roadmap still shows `running` because outbox rows were delayed or lost. Extend the storage claim: outbox append atomicity, drain CAS/ordering, crash tests that kill either side, and projection behavior while the drain is stalled—or admit the ledger is not yet the SSOT for live status.

findings.criterion: (planning integrity for a Foreman-ready campaign that stays the SSOT for what is running)
findings.message: The intro claims a “nine-phase plan (Phases 0–3 spine… Phases 5–7… Phases 8–9)” while the body is ten labeled stages (Phase 1 = Phase 0 through Phase 10 = Phase 9). That is not cosmetic for a plan that advertises Stage-2 seed quality: wave counts, dependency claims, and “every phase serves a named criterion” become un-auditable. Normalize numbering and phase count before this is treated as Stage-1 lock material.

findings.criterion: Nothing spent, written, or started without human confirmation
findings.message: Treating every gate answer as a full propose→confirm micro-commission unifies `who` and idempotency, but success criteria only name commission-before-spend and start-before-run—not mid-run gate UX as a second product surface. If Crucible has three approve gates plus budget re-confirms, John may face nested confirm stacks the North Star never described. Either add an explicit success criterion for mid-run gate confirmation (and friction budget), or distinguish “confirm spend/start” from “answer engine gate” while still recording principal—without forcing gate answers through commission_hash/step binding that may not apply.

findings.topic: static gate pre-answer may cover nothing
findings.criterion: Driven by talking/confirmation; no auto path that spends or advances without John
findings.message: Pre-answering is limited to exact sha256 match of rendered text and forbidden for the three Crucible approval gates. If those gates (and most Foreman blockers) embed dynamic project content, the optimization set may be empty—fine as optimization, dangerous if any later wave assumes reduced human load. Phase 0 should report how many inventoried gates are truly static after real renders; Phase 10 must not imply pre-answer contributes to acceptance of criteria 2–5.
